npc.krethon: Krethon, a Greek soldier in his forties with a weathered sun-browned face, a short greying dark beard, deep creases at the eyes, wearing a plain worn leather-and-bronze cuirass over a faded red tunic, a length of knotted cord tied at his belt with nine knots
npc.quartermaster: an older Greek quartermaster with grey stubble, a sun-leathered bald head, a plain undyed wool tunic, a wax tablet tucked under one arm
npc.sentry: a Trojan boy of about ten, dark-haired, in a dusty tunic, peering down from atop the pale limestone city wall

clips.scene: She stands on a wide sandy beach at first light, beached Greek ships with furled sails stretching away down the shore in both directions, the pale limestone walls of Troy visible far off on the upshore-left horizon. clips.dialogue: "The Trojan War. Homer says: ten years, a thousand ships, one big wooden horse. I'm here to fact-check the most famous story ever told. Rule one — stay off the plain."

Quartermaster pauses mid-step, not looking back: "Water to the shield line at dawn. Stay low." She looks after him, then turns her face to the lens, unreadable.

clips.timeOfDay: Day 2, dawn, harsh low early sun, long shadows, scene fully lit despite low sun angle
clips.scene: Inside a staggering line of soldiers advancing along the shield wall at the edge of the open plain (walls of Troy visible upshore-left in the distance), she is moving with them, serving water from a SOFT ANIMAL-HIDE WATERSKIN — a real Bronze Age water-bearer's implement made from a single small goat/kid hide: an irregular, lumpy, asymmetric silhouette (NOT a smooth round ball, NOT a symmetrical pillow), with visible hand-stitching along one seam and small knotted tie-off points at its lower edges where the hide was closed. A leather cord loops from the bag's gathered, tied neck up and over one shoulder, so the bag's weight hangs from the strap against her side/hip rather than being gripped overhead. A short wood-and-bronze pour-spout is fitted into the tied neck for controlled serving — matches the approved reference image supplied with this prompt exactly. She grips the spout with one hand, tilting it down toward a soldier's cupped hands beside her, water streaming out in a thin, controlled pour — her arm bent at a natural mid-height, NOT raised overhead. As she pours, an arrow streaks in from the side — visible for a brief instant as a fast blurred shaft crossing the frame — and thuds into the flat side of the hanging waterskin, the arrowhead punching through the soft leather at that single point, the shaft staying lodged there, protruding outward. A soldier beside her grabs her shoulder and hauls her down behind the shield line in the same motion — not two separate events, the pull is a continuation of the same forward motion, embedded not sequential. She keeps hold of the waterskin by its strap (arrow still fixed in the same puncture point) as she is pulled down.
clips.dialogue: Soldier, hauling her down, urgent: "Water girl! DOWN!" She, crouched low, flat delivery to the lens, catching her breath: "Okay. That's new."
clips.action: One continuous physical thread: she is already moving/serving water when the arrow hits and the pull-down happens as a variation of that same motion, per creative-direction.md §7. HOLDING/CARRY REQUIREMENT — CRITICAL (v4's render showed her incorrectly hoisting the entire waterskin overhead with both arms raised, gripped by its round body — physically awkward and flagged by the owner as wrong; fixed via a researched reference image supplied with this prompt, follow it exactly): the waterskin hangs from its own shoulder-strap cord against her side/hip, bearing its own weight; she operates it one-handed at the wood-and-bronze pour-spout, tilting only the spout toward the soldier — she never lifts the whole bag above shoulder height, never grips it two-handed overhead. SHAPE/MATERIAL REQUIREMENT — CRITICAL, NON-NEGOTIABLE (this prop has been rendered wrong three times already — rigid ceramic jar twice, then a shape too smooth and featureless to read as a genuine leather vessel the third time despite not being ceramic; researched from real Bronze Age/Near-Eastern waterskin construction and matched to the approved reference image supplied with this prompt — follow that reference image's exact bag shape, stitching, tie-points, strap, and spout): the bag is a whole small-hide construction — irregular, lumpy, asymmetric, with a visible hand-stitched seam and knotted tie-off points at its lower edges, a gathered tied neck, and a fitted wood-and-bronze pour-spout. It is NEVER pottery, NEVER ceramic, NEVER a hard clay jar, NEVER a rigid vessel, NEVER a smooth symmetrical ball or plain featureless pillow. It NEVER has a wide open mouth or visible hollow interior at any point in the clip. ARROW FLIGHT REQUIREMENT — CRITICAL (a prior render had the arrow appear already-embedded with no visible incoming motion, a confirmed error): the arrow must be visible in flight for at least 2-3 frames immediately before impact — a fast blurred shaft crossing into frame from the side — so the strike reads as a visible impact event, not a sudden appearance. OBJECT-PERSISTENCE REQUIREMENT — CRITICAL, NON-NEGOTIABLE: once the arrow punctures the flat side of the waterskin, the arrow shaft stays fixed at that exact single puncture point, protruding outward, for the ENTIRE REMAINDER of the clip, in every single frame the waterskin appears in — while she is pulled down, while crouching, in every close-up, in the final frame. The arrow does not disappear, does not relocate, does not end up resting inside any cavity (there is none), and does not detach. If it visibly breaks or shortens under the impact of the pull-down, the broken stub remains fixed at that same exterior puncture point — it does not fall inward or appear loose inside the bag. This is a single continuous take with no cuts — the waterskin, its shoulder strap and spout, and the arrow's exact puncture point must persist with perfect continuity exactly like her wardrobe, her hair, and every other physical detail already locked in this prompt.
clips.sound: arrow thud, shouting, shield clatter, wind

clips.scene: Sitting at a small campfire with {krethon}, the amber sunset sky bright behind the beached ships in silhouette, firelight warm on both their faces as accent light only. He holds a length of knotted cord, one knot per season — nine knots.
clips.dialogue: {krethon}, turning the cord slowly in his fingers: "The food was better the first three years." A pause. Quieter, looking at the cord not at her: "He walks now. My son. Somewhere... he walks." She takes the cord gently, says nothing, holds it. Silence. DO NOT RUSH — this silence is the entire beat.

clips.timeOfDay: Day 3, midday, bright direct sun, scene fully lit
clips.scene: Camp noise dies in a wave as a Greek champion — a lean, battle-hardened warrior with a distinct crested bronze helmet and finer, more ornate bronze cuirass than the rank-and-file soldiers around him (elite gear, still matte and battle-worn, NOT glam/fantasy shiny) — approaches at the head of a small group of Myrmidon soldiers in the background for scale. NO other named companion is present in this clip — it is just her and him. She walks normally forward on her own initiative toward him (facing her direction of travel, camera swinging to re-aim as she moves, not walking backward, per creative-direction.md §14), closing the distance herself until she is close enough for a real face-to-face exchange. He stops, turns to her, and actually answers — a genuine two-way conversation, both people looking directly at each other. He only begins walking away once she has FULLY finished her final line to the lens — he must still be in frame, stopped, while she delivers it.
clips.dialogue: She, walking straight up to him, direct, saying his name as recognition the moment she's close enough — this is the ONLY place his name is ever spoken in the whole episode, it must be clearly audible: "Achilles." A brief beat, then straight into: "Nine years. They say you could end this war tomorrow, if you fought. Why don't you?" Achilles stops, looks directly at her, flat and solemn: "Agamemnon took what was mine. I won't hand him my sword too." A beat — he holds her gaze, then turns and walks on. She watches him go, then turns to the lens, quiet, genuinely shaken (not smiling, not neutral — this line is fear, played real): "That's not strategy. That's a grudge with an army behind it. I have never been more scared of anyone in my life."
clips.action: Active-participant per §12: SHE approaches and initiates the whole exchange on her own, not standing beside someone else who does it for her, including saying his name herself. Real two-way conversation per the direct-address floor: she asks, he answers, she reacts to the lens after he's gone. Achilles' spatial staging must actually support eye contact and being heard: close enough for a normal speaking exchange. CRITICAL PACING NOTE: this dialogue is short by design — do NOT rush it to fill the clip's duration. Let real pauses breathe: a small beat after she says his name before her question, a beat before he answers, a held silent moment of eye contact before he turns to leave, and a clear beat after he starts walking away before she turns to the lens. Her final line is the emotional point of the whole clip and must be delivered at a natural, unhurried pace with a genuinely frightened/shaken expression — she must not still be talking while he's already walked far into the background, and her face must not read as calm, pleasant, or smiling.
clips.sound: camp noise dropping to near-silence as she approaches him, footsteps/armor clink close now, wind, silence under his lines and under her final line

FIRE-ARROW REQUIREMENT — CRITICAL, NON-NEGOTIABLE (a prior render showed a background flaming projectile as a vertical column launching straight up from the ground with a thick smoke plume stacked beneath it, reading exactly like a modern rocket liftoff — this is WRONG and must not recur): every visible flaming projectile in this clip is a single small arrow — a thin shaft with a flame wrapped around its head, trailing a short comet-like streak of fire and thin smoke behind it as it moves. It travels on a LOW, ARCING, PARABOLIC path, entering the frame at an angle from off-screen and continuing across the sky at a shallow angle, the way a shot arrow naturally arcs under gravity. It is NEVER a vertical column of fire launching straight up from a fixed point on the ground. It NEVER produces a thick, billowing, smoke plume stacked at one ground location. It NEVER resembles a rocket, missile, or spacecraft launch — no sustained upward thrust flame, no expanding exhaust cloud, no launch-pad silhouette. Each fire-arrow stays small and brief in frame, a background detail crossing the sky in under a second, not a large sustained pillar of flame that persists in one place. SMOKE TRAIL REQUIREMENT — CRITICAL, NON-NEGOTIABLE (the arcing flight path fixed one confirmed defect, but the trailing smoke itself was THEN separately confirmed by Gemini eyes as still reading as rocket-like: 'a thick, continuous gray smoke contrail that mimics the exhaust trajectory of a modern rocket' — this is a distinct problem from the trajectory and must be fixed too): the smoke trailing each fire-arrow is thin, wispy, sparse, and broken/discontinuous — like the faint trail behind a single thrown torch or burning stick, made of a few loose wisps, not a line. It is NEVER thick, NEVER opaque, NEVER billowing, NEVER a continuous solid-looking line, and NEVER the same visual weight or prominence as the small flame head itself — the flame head is the visually dominant part, the smoke is a faint secondary wisp. If the smoke trail is thick or solid enough to look like a jet contrail or rocket exhaust plume, the generation is WRONG. DUSK SKY REQUIREMENT — CRITICAL, NON-NEGOTIABLE (a prior render opened this clip with a bright blue daytime sky instead of the required dusk continuation from clip 9 — this is WRONG and must not recur): from the very first frame through the entire clip, the sky is a warm, saturated dusk gradient — deep orange near the horizon fading up into dusky blue-purple higher up, matching a sun that has just set or is about to. It is NEVER a bright, clear, saturated midday or afternoon blue sky, and it is NEVER pale or washed-out daytime-bright, not even for the opening beat before the raid escalates. The overall light stays warm and low-angle throughout, consistent with the fire ring's flicker being a plausible light source on her face. If any frame's sky reads as bright blue daytime rather than warm dusk, the generation is WRONG.

clips.scene: On the morning beach with {krethon}, she presses the nine-knot cord back into his hand.
clips.dialogue: "Get home, Krethon. Count them out loud to him." A warm beat between them. He nods, turns, walks off toward the ships. She watches a moment, then turns to the lens, warm and unhurried: "In three thousand years, a man finds this city with a shovel in one hand and Homer in the other." A small pause. "The poem is the MAP." Another beat. "Whether it happened like the song says — it happened for THEM." Softest smile: "Hazel — out of time."
clips.action: Warm, sincere outro register — unguarded, no jokes, gentle smile on the sign-off line. CRITICAL PACING NOTE: this is the episode's final spoken beat and it was rushed in an earlier pass — measured at 6.4 words/second, nearly double natural conversational pace. Every sentence here gets its own real breath and a small pause before the next one begins; nothing is delivered back-to-back without a beat. This is reflective and warm, closer to a slow exhale than a summary being read aloud. Do NOT compress the dialogue to fit the runtime — let the runtime serve the pacing, not the other way around.
